sections.heading: What is Net Revenue Retention (NRR)?
paragraphs: Net Revenue Retention (NRR), also called Net Dollar Retention (NDR), measures how much recurring revenue you retain and grow from existing customers over a specific period.

The simplest way to think about NRR: How much would your revenue grow or shrink if you acquired zero new customers? According to research, SaaS companies with high NRR grow 2.5x faster than low-NRR counterparts.

bullets.label: Predicts Sustainable Growth
bullets.text: Companies with NRR above 110% can grow significantly without new acquisition

bullets.label: Investor Priority
bullets.text: Often the single most important metric after revenue growth for VCs

bullets.label: Cost Efficiency
bullets.text: Expanding existing customers costs 5x less than acquiring new ones

bullets.label: Product-Market Fit
bullets.text: NRR above 100% indicates customers see enough value to invest more

sections.heading: How to Calculate NRR: The Formula
paragraphs: For example, with $100 starting MRR , $100 expansion , $100 contraction , and $100 churn :
sections.formula: NRR = (Starting MRR + Expansion - Contraction - Churn) / Starting MRR × 100

sections.heading: NRR by Average Contract Value (ACV)
paragraphs: Higher ACV correlates with higher NRR due to stickier enterprise customers.

sections.heading: NRR vs GRR
paragraphs: Both metrics matter but measure different things:
Why track both: A strong upsell motion can mask underlying retention problems. If NRR is 110% but GRR is 70%, you have a serious churn problem that expansion is covering up.

bullets.label: NRR
bullets.text: Includes expansion. Shows total growth potential from existing customers

bullets.label: GRR (Gross Revenue Retention)
bullets.text: Excludes expansion. Reveals core retention without upsells masking churn

bullets.label: Reduce Churn
bullets.text: Improve onboarding, proactive customer success, and cancel flow optimization

bullets.label: Drive Expansion
bullets.text: Upsell higher tiers, add seats, cross-sell new products, usage-based pricing

bullets.label: Reduce Contraction
bullets.text: Monitor usage drops, intervene before downgrades, demonstrate value continuously

bullets.label: Target Enterprise
bullets.text: Higher ACV customers have stickier contracts and more expansion potential
